newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AMP doubts Australia airport profit potential.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AMP doubts Australia airport profit potential.

text.p: One of the bidders for Australia's major airports on Monday cast doubt on their potential for increased profitability.
"There are very few easy cost savings there," Graham Timms, head of infrastructure investments for the Australian Mutual Provident Society (AMP), told Reuters.
A privatisation usually puts a greater value on a government business than is justified by its current profitability, because the buyer reckons it can implement additional savings.
But Timms said the government's main interest in the privatisation would be avoiding the bad investments to which its own managers were prone.
"The major benefit to the government is going to be preventing the wrong decisions in the future," Timms said.
"I don't think there is much in the way of staff numbers (to be cut)," he said. "But I think that the way the staff are allocated is relatively inefficient."
AMP, BAA Plc and pension investor State Super of New South Wales are jointly bidding for long leases on three airports -- Melbourne, Brisbane and Perth.
The value of the government's entire portfolio is estimated at A$2 billion to A$3 billion but the sale of Sydney airport, Australia's busiest, has been deferred.
The Federal Airports Corp, the current owner of the airports, made an operating profit of A$160 million in the year to June.
Tenders for the three airports currently on offer closed last week and details of the bids will be published later this month, with a decision to follow later in the year.
Timms said Australian airports tended to have too much investmented in new capital, sometimes before old capital was fully used.
A transfer to private interests would prevent the government putting its money into such poor investments.
